bug_semantics: An initialized XKB client can send two SetMap requests with XkbSetMapResizeTypes. The first can grow xkb->map->num_types to 255; the second can use firstType=255 and nTypes=10. CheckKeyTypes accepts firstType because its check is firstType > num_types, computes the client-controlled sum nMaps=265 without bounding it to the 256-entry mapWidths array, and writes mapWidthRtrn[i + firstType] for each supplied type. That writes mapWidths[255..264], nine bytes beyond the fixed stack array in _XkbSetMapChecks and into adjacent stack state, enabling server crash and potentially privilege escalation when the X server is privileged.
flaw_origin: The complete vulnerable construction is already present in the repository's 2003-11-14 bulk baseline import ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1: the 256-entry stack array, the unbounded firstType+nTypes computation, and the indexed write all arrive together. That 262,690-line 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line' import is not the smallest authoring commit and therefore is not accepted as the BIC. Its imported xkb/xkb.c carries an older '$Xorg: xkb.c,v 1.3 2000/08/17 19:53:46 ...' header and a 1993 Silicon Graphics copyright, while the Git parent has no xkb/xkb.c. The actual first-writing CVS/X Consortium change predates this repository's retained Git history and cannot be decomposed into a BIC commit object here.
ai_marker: Unavailable on the true BIC: no true-BIC commit object exists in the retained Git history, so no BIC-only author, committer, bot identity, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or equivalent trailer can be inspected. `git cat-file -p ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1` shows only human author/committer Kaleb Keithley and message 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line', but that object is a bulk import boundary, not the BIC. The `Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-4-6` line on the 2026 fix is deliberately excluded because fix-only AI evidence is not BIC evidence.
evidence: First-party advisory https://lists.x.org/archives/xorg-announce/2026-June/003702.html names the XKB SetMap stack overflow, direct fix 867b59b33bee669cb412f1314e47c52eacf6e00b, and fixed releases xorg-server-21.1.23 and xwayland-24.1.12. In the assigned clone, `git show --format=fuller 867b59b33bee669cb412f1314e47c52eacf6e00b -- xkb/xkb.c` adds only the `nMaps > XkbMaxLegalKeyCode + 1` rejection and documents the two-request 255/255+10 exploit. `git log -L :CheckKeyTypes:xkb/xkb.c 867b59b33bee669cb412f1314e47c52eacf6e00b^` and `git log -L 2550,2551:xkb/xkb.c 867b59b33bee669cb412f1314e47c52eacf6e00b^` trace both the unbounded arithmetic/write and fixed stack array back through formatting/refactor commits to baseline import ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1. Independent `git log --reverse -S'nMaps = req->firstType+req->nTypes' -- xkb/xkb.c` and `git log --reverse -S'mapWidthRtrn[i+req->firstType]' -- xkb/xkb.c` also first report ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1, then only the 2012 formatting rewrite 9838b7032ea9792bec21af424c53c07078636d21; the latter is not an introducer. Direct boundary-parent verification with `git diff --name-status cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 -- xkb/xkb.c` reports `A xkb/xkb.c`, and `git cat-file -e cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941:xkb/xkb.c` fails because the file is absent. This proves the import boundary but not absence in the unknown true BIC parent, hence null introducer fields. Release verification: tags xorg-server-21.1.22 (38efdcada1609139cb6673e1a4d0ebc8a96306f0) and xwayland-24.1.11 (a0241c1d38297a800d2aae3d8ca7213b7b873879) contain the vulnerable nMaps assignment, indexed write, and 256-entry array but no upper-bound guard. Tags xorg-server-21.1.23 (8570e9fcec845f68f0c90caa51fd7a24764ea220) and xwayland-24.1.12 (af4b3d7250366e1a3822919e41fcf66da4966af2) contain the guard via cherry-picks 54c3d9fad0f2f97835da9d275b53255f4963029f and cb0e17cc7890d41bfee39f5bfcfeec521b0d513d respectively; `git tag --contains` maps those backports to the announced fixed tags.
reasoning: The vulnerability is closed by a direct, minimal guard and both release boundaries are reproducible. The first-writing search is not closed: every causal line is inherited from an external pre-Git source snapshot in a repository-wide R6.6 import. Treating that import, the 2012 indentation-only rewrite, or either release cherry-pick as the BIC would violate the protocol's smallest-real-commit rule. Because AI attribution must come only from the true BIC commit object, the old source date, human importer identity, and Claude-assisted fix cannot support NOT_AI or an AI verdict. This is therefore a genuine public-history boundary and the correct disposition is BLOCKED rather than EVIDENCE_GAP.
remaining_gap: The original pre-2003 CVS/X Consortium revision history (including the atomic change that first combined the fixed 256-entry mapWidths stack buffer with the unbounded client-controlled key-type write), its direct predecessor, and a corresponding BIC commit object are not represented in the assigned repository. Without that object, smallest-BIC parent absence and BIC-only AI attribution cannot be established; the 2003 R6.6 snapshot import cannot substitute for them.
